name: The Grave Circle
summary: A ring of upright slabs round four shaft graves, the old kings' burial ground, walled in by the new kings' citadel.
description: Before there was a citadel there were these graves, and when the citadel was built its lords were careful to wall them in rather than build over them: four shafts cut into the rock, each capped with a stone slab, and round them a ring of upright stones topped with flat ones, a fence to keep the dead in. The ring has four gaps where the passages run through, and in each gap a draught that smells of old earth. The families still leave gold cups on the covers. They are still there.
source: Grave Circle A at Mycenae (plan and ring)
build: Shell: the kit's Crypt shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m limestone walls 3.00 m clear, 0.45 m ashlar capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 2.16 m centred on every wall.
Ring: 24 upright limestone slabs 0.60 m wide (tangential) × 0.20 m thick × 1.00 m tall, on a circle of radius 5.00 m about the cell centre.
Arcs: six uprights per quadrant at 25°, 33°, 41°, 49°, 57° and 65° from the east–west axis, so each arc stops short of the axes and the clear cross runs through the four gaps.
Cap slabs: flat ashlar slabs 0.30 m wide × 0.12 m, each bridging a neighbouring pair of uprights, top at 1.42 m above ground.
Shaft grave covers: four ashlar slabs 1.20 × 0.80 × 0.20 m at (±2.70, ±2.70), inside the arcs.
Gold cups: one on each cover, r 0.08 → 0.05 × 0.10 m, 0.30 m west of the cover's centre.
Floor: the Crypt's dark floor; earth darker inside the ring (albedo only).
Nothing stands in the cross: between the arcs and the archways is open floor.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.16 m (Crypt), all open
Ring gaps: four, on the axes, each at least 3.2 m wide

materials.name: Limestone
materials.notes: Walls and the uprights; weathered, rounded at the top.

materials.name: Dressed ashlar
materials.notes: Cap slabs, grave covers, capstone band.

materials.name: Gold
materials.notes: The cups on the covers: loot.

gameplay: Four gold cups in plain sight on the covers: easy loot, and the ring's uprights are the only cover.
The ring is waist-to-chest high (1.42 m): a crouching player can hide behind it from the archways.
The four gaps funnel movement across the room along the axes.
